title: Interactive tiled canvas mode
summary: Add a View-menu Tiled Mode that previews repeated copies of the active canvas and maps drawing on any copy back to the shared source artwork.

questions.question: Did 9×9 mean 81 copies or a 3×3 grid totaling nine?
questions.answer: Three canvases per row and column.
questions.decision: Default to 3 columns by 3 rows, totaling nine copies.

questions.question: Are copies passive or interactive with source-edge wrapping?
questions.decision: Map supported tool input on any copy to one source with positive modulo coordinates.

questions.question: Which tools may operate through surrounding copies?
questions.decision: Support pencil, eraser, mirror, dither, line, rectangle, circle, fill, and picker everywhere; restrict selection transforms to the source tile.

questions.question: How is tile count configured and persisted?
questions.decision: Provide independent 2–9 axes, 2×2/3×3/5×5 presets, device persistence, and a warning above 5 on either axis.

questions.question: Which platforms and adjacent view/export behavior are included?
questions.answer: All platforms; accept the proposed boundaries.
questions.decision: Support desktop, tablet, and phone; repeat grid/checker/onion skin, keep Live Preview singular, and leave exports/project data unchanged.

dependencies.reason: Completed shared View-menu architecture is the command surface for Tiled Mode on desktop and touch.

risks: Naively recomposing, cloning, or mutating once per visual copy could reintroduce severe large-canvas drawing lag.
Pointer, brush, mirror, dither, and shape coordinates can wrap incorrectly at negative edges, corners, zoom levels, or non-center copies.
A separate shape-preview path can disagree with samples committed at a wrapped seam.
Selection transforms on repeated copies could corrupt source pixels if source-tile gating happens after state mutation.
Repeated-surface resize can shift wheel, pinch, fit, or hand-pan focus unexpectedly.
Large configurable grids can overflow or become unusable on phone and tablet layouts.
Preference hydration races could overwrite saved values, dirty projects, or leak presentation state into files and exports.
A continuous CSS checker phase or flattened composite can make repeated copies differ in checker, onion, or opacity presentation.
validation: Unit-test positive modulo, layout/source-tile selection, display mapping, brush expansion, and wrapped/deduplicated raster samples across negative coordinates, all edges, and corners.

Playwright-test shared View commands, editor-only Shift+T versus Dither, 3×3 default rendering, every supported tool, seam preview/commit equality, one-step undo, source-only selection, settings validation, persistence, and dirty/export neutrality.
Verify checkerboard, grid, onion skin, opacity, and one singular Live Preview repeat or remain independent according to the specification.

Run desktop, 412×839 phone, 820×1180 tablet, and phone-landscape interaction and full-size snapshot QA for menu/dialog bounds, touch input, zoom focus, fit, hand pan, safe areas, and custom scrollbars.

Instrument a representative 120×120 default tiled stroke to verify one scheduled source composition per frame, bounded blits, no pointer-time canvas resize, and no per-tile editor mutation, project clone, or pixel traversal.
Run studio lint, typecheck, unit tests, static build, full Playwright suite, spec validation, Prettier, and git diff checks.
validationEvidence: Studio lint and typecheck passed; 48 Vitest tests passed; static Nuxt build passed; full Playwright suite passed 37/37; focused desktop tiled workflow, touch menu/dialog, and 120x120 mobile 3x3 performance tests passed; tiled workspace and settings snapshots were inspected at full size.
